title: Apollo vs Lusha for HubSpot Enrichment — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Apollo vs Lusha for HubSpot Contact Enrichment
description: Apollo or Lusha for a small HubSpot team: free plans, self-serve prices, what syncs into HubSpot, and who has to connect it.
h1: Apollo vs Lusha for enriching HubSpot contacts
dek: Both tools find emails and phone numbers. They differ in how much of HubSpot they touch.
Prices and integration details come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This is for a small team, a handful of reps, using HubSpot as its CRM and needing better contact data: work emails, direct dials, company details. You've narrowed it to Apollo and Lusha because both have free plans and prices you can see.
If you need a full data platform with intent data and a sales contract, look at a broader roundup instead. This page is about getting good contact data into HubSpot without a big project.

Pick Apollo if you want one tool that finds contacts, runs outreach, and keeps HubSpot in sync both ways. Pick Lusha if you want a simpler tool that reveals contact details and pushes them into HubSpot without creating duplicates.
Both need an admin to connect. Check that before you start a trial.

Apollo has a free plan that stays free with no time limit. Basic is $49 a month on monthly billing and Professional is $99 a month on monthly billing. Keep in mind that all seats on an Apollo account are on the same plan, so one power user can push the whole team up a tier, and unused credits expire at the end of each billing cycle.

Lusha has a Free plan with up to 40 credits a month, CRM integrations included. Starter is $49.90 a month billed monthly, with 400 credits a month, or $37.45 a month billed annually ($449.10 a year). Professional is $69.90 a month billed monthly, with 600 credits a month. Credits: 1 credit to reveal an email and 5 credits to reveal a phone number, so phone-heavy teams burn credits faster. Self-serve stops at a point: teams larger than 5 users go through sales.

sections.label: What each one does in HubSpot

blocks.html: Apollo's HubSpot integration offers two-way sync of contacts, accounts, and deals, with emails, calls, meetings, tasks, and notes pushed to HubSpot. Note that the HubSpot integration requires a paid Apollo subscription. You get 6 hours after enabling to set sync rules before anything syncs.

Lusha pushes contacts and companies into HubSpot with field mapping, and checks for existing records first so you don't create duplicates. It doesn't describe activity sync; it's built to get clean contact and company records into HubSpot.

So the real question is how much you want a second tool writing to HubSpot. Two-way sync is powerful, and it's also one more thing that can overwrite a field you care about. Set the mapping rules before you turn either one on.
For Apollo, connecting it takes a HubSpot super admin. For Lusha, setup needs admin access on both Lusha and HubSpot.
If your team doesn't have a HubSpot admin, that's your first step, not the tool choice. Whoever owns the HubSpot account has to approve the connection either way.
